explain.say: All day the desert ground soaks up strong sunshine. After sunset, the ground keeps giving out its heat as invisible infrared rays, and in a desert there is very little to stop them.

faq.q: Why does dry air let heat escape?
faq.a: Water vapour is a greenhouse gas: it absorbs infrared and sends some back to the ground. Dry desert air has little vapour, so the ground's heat escapes to space much more easily.
asks: Why is humid air warmer at night?

faq.a: Clouds absorb the heat the ground gives off and send much of it back down, like a blanket. On clear nights that heat escapes to space.
asks: Do clouds keep the ground warm?

faq.q: How cold can a desert get at night?
faq.a: Very cold. Desert nights can be 20 degrees or more cooler than the afternoon, and in winter parts of the Sahara and other deserts drop below freezing.
asks: Can it freeze in the desert?

faq.q: Why does sand heat up so fast in the day?
faq.a: Sand needs little energy to warm up, and it is a poor conductor, so the heat stays in its top layer. The surface gets scorching while a few centimetres down stays cool.
asks: Why is desert sand so hot?

faq.q: Why are humid places warm at night?
faq.a: In humid places the moist air and frequent clouds trap the heat given off by the ground, so nights stay warm and the temperature changes little.

facts: Deserts can swing by more than 20 degrees Celsius between the afternoon and the early morning.
Water vapour is the biggest contributor to the natural greenhouse effect that keeps Earth warm.
